questions.prompt: Is there anything you miss about your secondary school?

answers.basic: I miss the time after class when it was easy to see my friends. Now that everyone is working, even finding one evening that suits us can take a while. Back then we could decide to play badminton after school without checking anyone's calendar, which made getting together feel easy.

questions.prompt: What was your favourite subject at secondary school?

answers.basic: I liked maths because I enjoyed working out how to get from the question to the answer. I still get a similar feeling when I solve a problem at work. I liked questions where the first step wasn't obvious and a small clue suddenly made the rest of the problem fit together.

questions.prompt: Were there any subjects that you found difficult at secondary school?

answers.basic: English speaking was hard for me. I could work through a written question at my own speed, but it took me much longer to put an answer together out loud. I especially remember knowing the words I wanted on paper and then forgetting half of them when someone asked me a question.

questions.prompt: Do you remember your first day at secondary school?

answers.basic: I remember being a little nervous because I knew very few people. Once I found my classroom and talked to the person next to me, I felt more at ease. I don't remember what the first lesson was about, but I remember how relieved I was to have someone to talk to.
